name: How long does it take to hang, tape, and finish basement drywall?

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to hang, tape, and finish basement drywall?

acceptedAnswer.text: Finishing basement drywall typically takes one to two weeks for an average-sized residential basement. The schedule depends primarily on total square footage, ceiling height, and drying conditions between compound coats. The workflow begins with hanging drywall sheets, followed by taping joints and applying three successive coats of joint compound. In Colorado basements, where humidity is often low, joint compound can dry relatively quickly, but each coat still requires adequate curing time before sanding. Once sanding creates a smooth surface, primer and finish paint can be applied. Unexpected framing irregularities, extensive soffit build-outs around ductwork, or moisture issues can extend this timeframe.
